FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A45
Paint on the road splits lanes, sets passing and lane-change permission, points turn lanes, marks stop lines and carves walkways, together steering lane control. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A45
Edge lines trace the road rim, solid white guarding the right shoulder and solid yellow the left rim of divided streets. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A45
Same-way lanes part on white, dashed white inviting a safe lane change and solid white ordering drivers to hold their lane short of special cause. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A45
Yellow centers split opposing flows, dashed yellow pairing single opposing lanes where passing stands open, while yield lines flag must-yield ground such as mid-block crossings. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A46
Where dashed yellow runs beside solid, only the broken side may pass, the solid side stays put. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A46
Twin solid yellow stripes crown the middle of two-way roads, crossed solely to swing left into or out of alleys, private roads, driveways and streets. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A46
Signs and signals demand a halt ahead of the stop line, crosswalks fence the walkers’ zone where drivers yield to feet inside or stepping in, and unmarked crossings still hide walkers at every corner. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A46
Reserved lanes announce themselves by signs and white diamonds, transit or bus for buses alone, bicycle for bikes alone, and diamond HOV lanes for cars meeting the posted rider count. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A46
Shared middle lanes serve left turns both ways, U-turns where lawful, under alternating turn arrows between solid and dashed yellow walls, sometimes flipping reversible at rush, so enter only when the way reads safe. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A46
Reversible lanes swap direction by hour inside double-dashed yellow, so read the signs and lamps first: green arrow ride it, red X shun it, blinking yellow X turns only, steady yellow X clear out soon. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A46
Odd paint warns too: diagonal stripes cage fixed blocks, solid lines funnel past hazards, twin solid white bars any lane swap, curbs and fire lanes may ban parking by local order, and a sharrow’s chevrons over a bike mark a shared lane to watch for riders. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A47
Red commands a full stop until green returns with the crossing empty, though right turns may roll after halting, scanning oncoming traffic, honoring any no-turn sign and sparing the walkers ahead. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A47
Yellow warns red is next, so brake when safe, but a car already inside the crossing when yellow dawns must roll on through. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A47
Green opens the crossing with duties attached: bow to emergency rigs and legal rivals, drain waiting cross traffic first, turn left only through a safe gap and yield right turns to crossing feet. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A47
A blinking red light equals a stop sign, halting fully before a safe entry, while blinking yellow just begs slower, warier rolling. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A47
Arrows aim the order: red arrow bars its heading until green arrow or lamp frees it, yellow arrow ends green-arrow shelter and counsels stopping, green arrow blesses the turn with cross and opposing lanes held. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A47
The HAWK beacon, a yellow eye beneath twin reds, wakes by walker button and freezes cars to a full stop until the crossing empties. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A47
Read the HAWK phases: dark means roll on, blinking yellow means a walker woke it, solid yellow means red approaches, solid red means feet in the street so stop, blinking red means stop then creep once the walkers clear as it sleeps. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A47
Signal heads speak stop and go, green for go-when-safe, yellow for caution, red for halt, usually stacked green, yellow, red from the ground up, though lone single-color lamps guard some spots. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
